title: A specified regular fibre sequence lifts on a principal neighbourhood
statement: Let $R\to A$ be flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $P\in\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(p)\otimes_R A)$ contract to $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If the image of a specified finite list $f$ of elements of $A$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in $(\kappa(p)\otimes_R A)_P$, there exists $g\notin Q$ such that its image is regular in $A[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, proof of assertion (1): successive application of Tag 062Y(3) to a specified fibre regular sequence.

proof.text: The fibre algebra is finite type over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, hence Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Apply [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] to the images of the chosen $f_j$ at $P$. Write its shrinking element as $a/r$ with $a\in A$ and $r\notin\mathfrak p$, and invert $a$. Since the shrinking element is outside $P$, $a$ is outside $Q$. The chosen equations are now a regular sequence on the whole fibre.

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, proof of (1), via Tag 062Y(3)

proof.text: Induct on $e$, the number of equations lifted. Retain a principal neighbourhood of $Q$ on which every prefix quotient through $e$ is flat and finitely presented over $R$, the first $e$ successive multiplications are injective, and all successive fibre multiplications remain injective. At $e=0$ flatness and finite presentation are the assumptions and principal localization preserves them. Under further localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identify all prefix quotients and fibres and preserve the injections.

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, proof of (1), via Tag 062Y(3)

proof.text: For the induction step, let f be the head of the list. Its multiplication on the whole fibre is injective. Apply the scalar criterion exists_notMem_forall_mul_mem_map, proved in the module of [lem-pc-algebra-fibre-cartier-local], with the second scalar equal to 1. It gives g outside the retained prime and uniform annihilator bounds modulo every base ideal. The same module's isRegularPrincipal_and_flat_of_forall_mul_mem_map makes f a nonzerodivisor on B=A[1/g] and makes C=B/(f) flat over R. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], the fibre of C is the quotient of the fibre of B by f, so the tail is weakly regular. Apply induction in C. Lift its new denominator through B onto C, and clear the denominator from A to B. The iterated localization is a principal localization of A. Quotient localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] identifies its tail quotient with the inductively chosen localization of C. Flat localization preserves the head injection [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] and base flatness (Mathlib flat localization and transitivity). Combine head and tail using the regular-sequence cons criterion.

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, proof of (1), via Tag 062Y(3)

proof.text: The image of the specified list in the fibre-local ring has proper ideal. Thus every equation lies in Q, and Q survives all shrinking elements. The final quotient is nonzero; the successive injections obtained by induction give regularity [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The empty list is regular since the prime survives. This proves the assertion on the canonical principal localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

lean.statement: theorem exists_isRegular_of_fiber_local (R A : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Module.Flat R A] [FinitePresentation R A] (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (Q : PrimeSpectrum A) (P : PrimeSpectrum (p.asIdeal.Fiber A)) (hP : P.comap TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom = Q) (fs : List A) (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime P.asIdeal) (fs.map fun a ↦ algebraMap (p.asIdeal.Fiber A) (Localization.AtPrime P.asIdeal) (TensorProduct.includeRight a))) : ∃ g : A, g ∉ Q.asIdeal ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.Away g) (fs.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away g)))
